entries.title: Breaking: /simplify renamed to /code-review
entries.paragraph: The slash command /simplify is gone. Use /code-review instead. The new command takes effort levels (low / medium / high) and can post findings directly as GitHub PR comments. Pinned background sessions also now stay alive when idle instead of timing out.
entries.whyItMatters: Any CI script, hook, or alias that types /simplify stops working today. One-line rename, but you have to ship it.

example.code:
# scan repo for stale references
rg -F '/simplify' .github scripts
# replace with /code-review medium

entries.title: Critical fix: Bash tool exit code 127 regression
entries.paragraph: Version 2.1.147 introduced a regression where every Bash command returned exit code 127 ("command not found"), making the Bash tool unusable. 2.1.148 fixes it. Anyone who auto-bumped past 2.1.146 should re-check that they did not get stuck on 2.1.147.
entries.whyItMatters: If your team uses Bash-heavy workflows and auto-updates Claude Code, a quiet day on 2.1.147 was actually a broken day. Bump to 2.1.148+ now.

entries.title: /usage per-category breakdown + markdown task lists in output
entries.paragraph: /usage now splits token spend by category (input / output / cache hits / tools). /diff got proper scrolling for big diffs. Assistant output renders GitHub-style markdown task lists (- [ ]) as interactive checkboxes. PowerShell security hardening on Windows.
entries.whyItMatters: Concrete budget visibility instead of a single opaque number — easy to see where the cache is or is not helping.

entries.title: /model is now session-only scope + /resume for background sessions
entries.paragraph: Changing the model with /model no longer persists across sessions — it applies to the current session only. To set the project default, edit settings. Background sessions can now be resumed with /resume, and the plugin marketplace shows richer plugin details.
entries.whyItMatters: Teams who relied on /model as a sticky preference will be surprised. Set the default in settings.json instead.

entries.title: Custom env var passthrough preserves SDK version headers
entries.paragraph: Supplying a custom env map to the SDK used to wipe out the SDK's own version/telemetry headers. Fixed in 0.3.149 — your custom env is merged with the SDK's defaults instead of replacing them.
entries.whyItMatters: If you scope env tightly (e.g. { PATH, HOME } only) the SDK now keeps its identifying headers, which Anthropic uses to triage support tickets.

entries.title: Parity with Claude Code 2.1.150
entries.paragraph: Roll-up release matching the underlying Claude Code 2.1.150 binary. No standalone SDK feature changes — bump to stay aligned with the CLI behavior changes from the week (renamed /simplify, /resume, /usage breakdown).
entries.whyItMatters: If you ship the Agent SDK in production and want users to get the same UX as the CLI, this is the version to pin.

entries.title: Goals on by default + foreground remote-control
entries.paragraph: Codex "Goals" (persisted completion conditions across turns) are now on by default with dedicated storage. codex remote-control now runs as a foreground command that waits for readiness and reports status — separate start / stop commands cover the daemon style. Permission profiles gained list APIs, inheritance, managed requirements.toml, and stronger Windows sandbox integration.
entries.whyItMatters: Goals = automatic guardrails on long sessions. Foreground remote-control means scripts no longer need readiness-polling hacks. Inherited permission profiles let teams ship one base profile and extend per project.

example.code:
# foreground mode (default now)
codex remote-control --workspace ./repo

# daemon mode
codex remote-control start --workspace ./repo
codex remote-control stop

entries.title: Python SDK auth + codex exec resume --output-schema
entries.paragraph: The Codex Python SDK now does first-class auth — API key, ChatGPT browser flow, device-code flow, account inspection, logout. codex exec resume accepts --output-schema, so resumed automations enforce JSON structure on the resumed turn. Faster TUI startup via batched terminal capability probes.
entries.whyItMatters: Schema-validated resumes plug a long-standing gap — long-running jobs survive interruptions without losing typed output guarantees.

entries.title: Unified @ picker + plugin marketplace CLI
entries.paragraph: @ mentions now search files, directories, plugins, and skills in one picker (backed by app-server metadata). TUI got service-tier commands, blended token usage, approval-mode display, and responsive Markdown tables. Plugin marketplace gained CLI commands, version-aware sharing, share checkout, and default-enabled plugin hooks.
entries.whyItMatters: One picker for every reference type drops the mental overhead of remembering which prefix attaches what. Marketplace CLI means plugin sharing finally fits into shell-based workflows.

entries.title: Visible plugin hooks + AWS console-login Bedrock auth
entries.paragraph: Plugin details now show every hook the plugin bundles before you install. Bedrock auth uses AWS console-login credentials via aws login profiles directly. App-server clients can page large threads with summary or full views.
entries.whyItMatters: Audit plugins for surprising hooks before installing instead of post-hoc. AWS users get a shorter setup path — no manual STS dance.

entries.title: API surface updates — types and helpers
entries.paragraph: Routine API spec sync — new response field types and helper updates pulled from the upstream OpenAPI spec. No removals; existing code keeps working. Safe to bump.
entries.whyItMatters: Stay current so TypeScript types match the live API shape. Skipping a release means missing new optional fields.

example.code:
npm i openai@^6.39.0
# or
bun add openai@^6.39.0

entries.title: service_tier parameter on responses compact
entries.paragraph: responses.compact() now accepts a service_tier parameter. Pass "priority" for latency-sensitive paths, "flex" for cost-sensitive batch jobs, or leave undefined for the account default.
entries.whyItMatters: Per-call tier selection is a direct cost / latency lever — important for services with mixed interactive and batch workloads.

entries.title: Realtime translate + web_search_call.results in responses
entries.paragraph: Launches the new realtime.translate endpoint and an updated image_2 model. The web_search_call.results include option on the Responses API now returns the raw search hits used by the model. Admin organization usage responses gained a quantity field.
entries.whyItMatters: Surfacing search results lets you display sources to the user (citations) instead of trusting the model's paraphrase blind.

entries.title: Per-endpoint Admin API Keys + admin metadata fields
entries.paragraph: Admin API Keys can now be scoped to specific endpoints instead of full org access. Admin resources gained group_type / user metadata fields. Several admin API update calls flow through more cleanly with typed responses.
entries.whyItMatters: Tightens the blast radius of admin keys — useful for ops tools that only need one operation, not full admin authority.

suggestions.title: Grep for /simplify across CI scripts and dotfiles before Monday
suggestions.paragraph: Claude Code 2.1.147 removed /simplify in favor of /code-review. Any GitHub Action, alias, hook, or runbook that invokes /simplify silently no-ops on a fresh CLI install.
suggestions.whyItMatters: Rename now while it's quiet. Wait until you need it in a fire-drill and it's a much worse moment to debug.

example.code:
rg -F '/simplify' .github .claude scripts docs
# replace each with: /code-review medium  (or high for security audits)

suggestions.title: Pin Claude Code minors in CI — skip 2.1.147
suggestions.paragraph: The 2.1.147 → 2.1.148 episode (Bash returning 127 on every command) is a textbook case for not auto-bumping the CLI in CI. Pin the patch version and bump deliberately.
suggestions.whyItMatters: An auto-bumped CI silently failing because every Bash step returns 127 is the worst kind of broken — green-looking, actually broken.

example.code:
# .github/workflows/claude.yml
- run: npm i -g @anthropic-ai/claude-code@2.1.149  # pin, do not float

suggestions.tiesTo: claude-code · v2.1.148 — Bash exit 127 regression fix

suggestions.title: Adopt Codex permission-profile inheritance for multi-project workspaces
suggestions.paragraph: Codex 0.133.0 added permission-profile inheritance and a managed requirements.toml. Define one base profile (network deny, fs scoped to project root) and have per-project profiles extend it instead of copy-pasting.
suggestions.whyItMatters: Single source of truth for tool permissions. New project = one short delta file, not a 50-line config you forgot to update.

example.code:
# ~/.codex/profiles/base.toml
[permissions]
network = "deny"
fs_write = ["$WORKSPACE"]

# ./project/.codex/profile.toml
[profile]
extends = "base"

[permissions]
network = "allow"  # this project needs it

suggestions.title: Route batch jobs through service_tier: "flex"
suggestions.paragraph: If your service has a batch path (overnight reports, bulk classification, async enrichment) that does not need interactive latency, pass service_tier: "flex" on Responses calls. The new SDK exposes it explicitly per call.
suggestions.whyItMatters: Flex pricing meaningfully undercuts the default tier for jobs that can tolerate slower turn-around. Easy lever, real money over a month.
suggestions.tiesTo: OpenAI Node SDK · v6.38.0 — service_tier on responses compact

suggestions.title: Surface web-search citations using web_search_call.results
suggestions.paragraph: Including web_search_call.results in your Responses API call returns the raw sources the model consulted. Display them next to the model's answer so users can verify claims rather than trusting paraphrase.
suggestions.whyItMatters: Public assistants live or die on perceived trustworthiness. Showing sources is cheap to ship and shifts user perception fast.
suggestions.tiesTo: OpenAI Node SDK · v6.37.0 — web_search_call.results include option
